I was heartbroken to hear this week that my friend Roman R Hudson passed away. I've known Roman for a few year, and I've had the pleasure of photographing him twice.

The first time I ever met Roman was in the middle of the Fort Lauderdale Airport. I saw a beautiful man with his massive beard and something in my memory clicked and connect him with photos that my friend Marc had posted from a recent beard competition. I worked up the nerve and walked up to say hello. We chatted a bit, connected on Facebook, and then continue on our journeys.

Then two years ago at IML, Roman reached out to me to photograph him in gear from P&C Creations. We found an out of the way spot in the alley behind the nearby theater, and with help from Bryan Patrick and Joseph J Deogracias, we captured this urban warrior.

And then last year at IML I spent an intimate hour with Roman and his partner Andy Frederick. The love these two clearly shared was immediately obvious.

As Roman's friends and family say goodbye to him on Saturday in Mississippi, please know that I am there in spirit.

Hi everyone. Sorry, I've been a bit distracted for the past few months with the marriage amendment volunteering, being sick for a while, and several other things.

I'm hoping to dust of the cameras in the next month, and I'm looking for volunteer models. Who's feeling adventurous?!?

My project this week is to get a small selection of my photos printed and framed to display at a booth at Twin Cities pride this weekend. Thank you to Bobbie Smith for giving me a few second hand frames he's been storing.

It's been a long time since I've printed and frames any photos. I don't think I can pull together the skills to cut new mats this week, so I've tracked down pre-cut mats at a few places that I'll check out over lunch tomorrow. If that goes well, then I'll head over to West Photo and see if I can get my photos printed. (Thank you Chuck Smith for that recommendation.)

It's always challenging to pick out the right photos to represent my work. I have ten years worth of leather event photos, but I'm moving more towards portraits now, so my selection for display will only include one event photo, which was the photo that was on the cover of Lavender last summer after Pride.

Sometimes I feel like my life is a video game, and there are certain moments when I "level up" in the game. That moment when all of the small hit points and character traits in life coalesce into a new awareness and expanded abilities.

This summer I feel like I leveled up in terms of looking at my creative work as a business. I feel like I'm approaching another business level up point.
Naked men aren't the only subject of my photographs. I just finished a fun little shoot with Bill and Jake's lovely dogs for a short walk along Lake Nokomis. We had some beautiful late afternoon sun.

I'm sad tonight because we lost a great man today. I'm thankful tonight because my Facebook feed is full of memories of Chuck Renslow, his life, and the legacy he leaves all of us. 

The first time I met Chuck was at the inaugural Mr. Wisconsin Leather contest in 2013. He journeyed up to Milwaukee to welcome this fledgling event to the IML family. The next year I met him again when he attended Iowa Leather Weekend. I was finally able to have a  conversation with him on his home turf at IML in 2015 during the LA&M President's Reception, and again at the same reception in 2016. We talked a bit about photography. :)

He created the contest event that goes a long way in defining the image of leather in our community. He founded the archives and museum that guards our history. And his pioneering male physique photography blazed the trail that I walk every time I photograph a naked man.  I owe my art to Chuck Renslow. 

Rest in peace, Chuck.
